title: Type Safety Patterns: Branded Types, Discriminated Unions & Exhaustiveness
description: Master enterprise TypeScript safety patterns: opaque branded types to prevent primitive confusion, discriminated union state machines, type guard functions, and exhaustive switch checking with the never type.

data.text: Eliminating Primitive Obsession with Branded Types

Enterprise code frequently passes raw strings representing domain concepts: user IDs, tenant IDs, document IDs, embedding vectors, and API keys. The type system sees them all as `string`, allowing catastrophic mixups like passing a `userId` where a `tenantId` is required. Branded (opaque) types enforce domain semantics at the type level without any runtime overhead.

data.title: Branded Nominal Types for Domain Identifiers
data.content: Using intersection with a unique brand symbol to create structurally distinct types from the same primitive.

data.text: React components managing multi-step workflows—like AI agent execution with human approval gates—often use 4–6 boolean flags that can combine into impossible states (e.g., `isLoading=false` while `isPendingApproval=true`). Discriminated unions eliminate invalid state combinations entirely.

data.title: Discriminated Union for Streaming Chat State
data.content: A union type that makes it impossible to be in contradictory states simultaneously.

data.text: Type Guard Functions for Runtime Validation
When receiving untyped JSON from SSE streams or external APIs, user-defined type guards validate the shape at runtime while narrowing the TypeScript type in subsequent code blocks.

data.title: Type Guard for SSE Event Parsing
data.content: Safely narrowing raw parsed JSON to specific SSE event types using is predicates.

data.caption: TypeScript Type Safety Patterns: Problems Solved
rows: Primitive confusion (passing userId where tenantId needed)
Argument order errors caught at compile time
TypeScript narrows type in each branch
Typing raw JSON from SSE/API without validation
Missing cases in switch statements as type grows
Compile error if new union member not handled
Magic number/string values scattered in code
Literal types instead of broad string/number

data.title: Type Safety Implementation Checklist
items: Replace raw string/number domain identifiers with Branded<T, Brand> types
Model multi-step async workflows as discriminated unions, not boolean flag combinations
Use the never exhaustiveness pattern in switch statements to catch missing union cases
Write user-defined type guard functions (is predicates) for all SSE and API JSON parsing
Enable TypeScript strict mode (strict: true) to activate all strictness checks
Use Zod or Valibot for runtime schema validation that automatically infers TypeScript types

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Branded types prevent domain primitive mixups with zero runtime cost.
Discriminated unions eliminate impossible component states by design.
Type guard functions bridge the gap between dynamic runtime values and compile-time types.
Next, we move to state management architecture: when to use Context, Zustand, or Redux Toolkit.
data.takeaway: The best bug is the one that never reaches production: TypeScript's advanced safety patterns transform class-of-bug eliminations into compile-time guarantees.
